judgements.justification: B's czKb made a wrong claim (Eq. (12) invalid) but kept 7, and it works against the gap; no score fell on it.
B's AC gave a spotlight on unanimous 7-8 ratings (mean 7.25); the scores support the tier.
B's QSy5 rated 8 on a review that repeats the paper's own conclusion with no specifics, lifting B's mean from 7.0 to 7.25.
No flaw was disclosed on one forum only; both committees saw the same parameter bias and missing baselines.
B's naZJ and czKb flagged the large Sec. 4.1 parameter error and no baselines, yet rated 7 and the AC listed them as camera-ready revisions.
Rebuttals moved scores up in both committees (A: 7pq7, 4Rfw; B: d46C).
One-sided issues exist on both sides, but none changed a score; the decisive faults are shared.
Both saw qualitative-only evaluation, no baseline and the parameter bias; B called them revisions at 7-8, A's reviewers held at 6 on them.
Neither AC adopted a single reviewer's position; both followed the scores.
No reviewer moved because of the other reviews.
The authors answered each reviewer; non-movement came from reviewers' silence (5o85, naZJ), not missed replies.
A's 5o85 gave a short 6 with one specific point and never replied, and 4Rfw's 1.5 h review was three questions; both 6s counted in the mean.
Both committees accepted, in line with their ratings.
No acceptance threshold was at stake; A's AC accepted, and its tier followed the mean.
A's lower scores are 6s, above threshold, and rest on central points (baselines, quantitative results).
Both committees read the paper as the same methodological contribution, the first VI framework for continuous-time hybrid systems.
No reviewer stated the core was outside their expertise and then rose on clarifications; earlier ratings are not public.
Both committees asked the same things of the paper (baselines, quantitative results, scaling); they differed in weight, not in requirement.
No praise rests on a checked wrong claim; QSy5 echoes the paper's conclusion but makes no specific false claim.
No below-threshold score was kept after its concern was answered.
No committee refused promised comparisons; the authors argued no hybrid baseline exists rather than promising one.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from an unedited score in a way the committee acted on.
No off-record extra reviewer.
Both committees found the exposition clear; expertise did not shape a clarity verdict.
4Rfw's text conditions acceptance on answers yet ends at 6, but the earlier rating is not public and 4Rfw replied, so a silent raise is not shown.
Neither AC set aside a silent detractor; A's silent 5o85 counted.
A had the detailed champion (x8VX, 8), and B also had a reviewer at 8, so the champion was not unique to one side.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading with high confidence.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical school.
B's meta-review argued only that the paper 'deserves acceptance' and gave no case for spotlight beyond the 7-8 scores.
Both committees saw the same baseline gap and the debt to Archambeau and Opper; literature knowledge did not split by committee.
A's meta-review omits x8VX's 8 but misstates no reviewer's final position.
No reviewer raised narrow audience or venue fit.
A's lower scores came from thin reviews, not a misreading detractor, and A's AC wrote no defence of acceptance.
No new experiments were posted to either forum; answers were arguments and promised figures.

added.name: Expert review outweighed by low-confidence reviews
added.definition: One committee's only high-confidence expert review rated the paper above its less-informed, lower-confidence reviewers, and the area chair followed the mean of ratings without weighing expertise, so the non-expert scores set the tier.
added.justification: R12 names a thin review counting unchallenged and R27 a champion present on one side only; neither names an expert's higher score being averaged away by lower-confidence reviews, the mechanism that set A's tier here.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same paper and the same faults: qualitative-only evaluation, no baseline, biased parameter estimates, linear drift. B's reviewers called them camera-ready work and rated 7-8, with one unargued 8, and B's AC gave a spotlight without a case beyond the scores (R08, R05, R03, R30). In A, three thin or non-expert 6s outweighed the only expert's 8, and the AC followed the mean (R12, new R36). R06 does not apply because rebuttals raised scores in both committees. R27 does not apply because B also had an 8. I added R36 because no reason names an expert review averaged away by lower-confidence ones.
